It builds on Stone’s foundational work on linear pooling and extends to Wallis’ variance decomposition, offering a principled measure of ensemble heterogeneity. In GSI, this translates to calibrated uncertainty quantification via proper scoring rules such as those introduced by Gneiting & Raftery (2007) and Gneiting (2012), which are essential for Bayesian inference. For GSE, the causal readiness report leverages stabilized sPoRT support maps to generate actionable diagnostics before effect estimation—this is a dual mechanism to linear pooling, where ensemble diversity informs both model confidence and causal validity. The feature recipe gate acts as a filter ensuring that only robust signals propagate into downstream models, preventing artifacts from spurious correlations. Together, these primitives form a triad of ensemble integrity, causal readiness, and signal robustness that enables adaptive decision-making in complex domains.
